issues: Both pages were grey wireframe placeholder dashboards with no content and no cause and effect, so there was nothing to make "seamless"
The occluder was an enlarged dark card smeared by 12-sample CameraMotionBlur plus four ghost layers: expensive, and it read as a grey smudge
The background needed bleed strips to cover the shove; there was no sense of depth, just a flat light-grey page
Nothing happened before the swipe, so the change had no motive
changes: Sand look (beige and terracotta) as a travel app: A is a desert-camp listing (860px procedural dune-sunset photo, 92px serif title, price, big terracotta Reserve button); B is the booking confirmation (168px serif "You're going.", a ticket stub and a terracotta check seal)

One causal line: Reserve is pressed at 24f (press scale, darken, Reserving… spinner), a defocused foreground object whips past, and the trip is booked; the layout flips sides, a big change that still reads as continuous (the ticket header reuses the dune photo)

The occluder is now an out-of-focus dark-brown foreground object grazing the lens: a gradient-only 2600px solid core with 340px soft edges (the edges are the defocus and motion blur), a terracotta rim on the leading edge and a soft shadow ahead; CameraMotionBlur is gone and the render is several times faster

One take: the content pans slowly from +40 to −40px across the cut; before the cut the wind drags it left, after it B settles from the right over 14f; the hard cut lands at 39f when the core covers the frame
After the cut the seal springs in (damping 13) and its check draws on, the details and confirmation code rise in stagger, then a 40f hold
